design_references.title: Fleet CPG Engine — Phase 4 (Prove generality)
design_references.claim: Add language #2 and watch the lowering layer, not the feature. Exit: language #2 requires zero changes below the lowering layer. Any change there means the IR boundary is wrong -- fix it now, not after five languages have calcified around the mistake. This experiment makes that mechanically checkable: a single shared core.py (store I/O, COW/LSM merge, L2 blast radius, packet materialization) is finalized against TypeScript first, then a Python lowering module is added, and core.py's sha256 is compared before and after.

hypothesis: A shared, language-agnostic core (store I/O, merge, blast radius, packet materialization) built and finalized against a TypeScript lowering module requires zero source changes to also support a Python lowering module on a real merged fastapi PR -- core.py's sha256 hash is bitwise identical whether the pipeline runs TypeScript or Python, and both produce facts that exactly match a from-scratch extraction at their respective commits.
null_hypothesis: Supporting Python requires any change to core.py (a different hash across runs, or a hash that no longer matches the file on disk), or either language's extracted facts diverge from a from-scratch ground-truth extraction.
independent_variable: Which lowering module drives the shared core -- typescript (zod, reproducing fleet-cpg-phase2-blast-radius-zod's small bucket as a regression check) vs. python (a real merged fastapi PR, genuinely new) -- holding core.py, the merge mechanism, and the blast-radius relation fixed.

environment.network_justification: git clone of zod and fastapi from github.com (fastapi already materialized from fleet-cpg-baseline-fastapi; zod from earlier fleet-cpg-* experiments). No other endpoints.

variants.name: typescript
variants.description: zod @ 5ff9566 (same small-bucket PR #6511 as fleet-cpg-phase2-blast-radius-zod) through core.py + lowering_typescript.py. A regression check: must reproduce that experiment's exact small-bucket numbers (merged_defs=1388, merged_calls=43888, impact_set_size=0).

variants.name: python
variants.description: fastapi @ d623544 (real merged PR #16105, 'Fix support for background tasks and headers from dependencies in app.frontend()', 1 file / 22 lines in fastapi/routing.py) through the identical core.py + a new lowering_python.py. The genuinely new case.

metrics.acceptance_rule: Accept: core_py_sha256 is identical across every repetition of both variants and matches the current core.py file on disk, the typescript variant reproduces fleet-cpg-phase2-blast-radius-zod's small-bucket numbers exactly, and the python variant's defs/calls match a from-scratch extraction on every repetition. Reject: any hash divergence, any correctness mismatch, or a typescript-variant number that fails to reproduce the prior experiment's result.

evaluator.rubric: Score on: (1) core.py's sha256 hash is identical across every TypeScript and every Python run, and matches the actual core.py file on disk at evaluation time -- not merely agreeing with itself, which would pass even if core.py had been silently edited after the recorded runs; this is the agnosticism gate's mechanical test, standing in for "language #2 requires zero changes below the lowering layer"; (2) the TypeScript variant reproduces fleet-cpg-phase2-blast-radius-zod's small-bucket numbers exactly (merged_defs=1388, merged_calls=43888, impact_set_size=0) as a regression check that refactoring the shared logic into core.py did not change behavior; (3) the Python variant, on a real merged fastapi PR, has defs and calls that exactly match a from-scratch extraction at that commit, proving the new lowering module is correct on real code, not just structurally present; (4) any single failure on either check -- a hash mismatch or a correctness mismatch -- fails the whole gate, since either one falsifies the IR-boundary claim this phase exists to test.
